claims.text: Al and Cr are reactive alloying elements suitable for modifying a lightweight HEA.
Targeted Al or Cr additions produce moderate lattice distortion in the HEA.
Moderate lattice distortion refines the microstructure through nanoscale precipitation.
The alloying additions form nanometer-scale precipitates.
The alloying additions promote surface segregation.
Reactive-element additions accelerate formation of a uniform and adherent protective oxide film.
The protective oxide film is self-healing.
Controlled lattice distortion and nanoscale precipitation provide precipitation strengthening.
The modified alloy will have higher yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have higher tensile strength than the baseline alloy.
The protective oxide film improves corrosion resistance.
The modified alloy will have a lower corrosion rate than the baseline alloy.
The protective oxide film improves resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
After high-temperature exposure, the modified alloy will have a more uniform, adherent, and slowly growing oxide film than the baseline alloy.
The reactive-element additions preserve the alloy's low density.
The baseline alloy has lower mechanical performance than the optimized modified alloy.
The baseline alloy has less effective oxide passivation than the optimized modified alloy.
The beneficial effects occur only within an optimal range of reactive-element concentrations.
Excessive reactive-element additions may produce brittle oxides.
Excessive reactive-element additions may form detrimental secondary phases that degrade mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation performance.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts that excessive additions will form brittle or detrimental phases and reduce performance, while the falsification rule treats that same behavior at excessive addition levels as falsifying the hypothesis. A result outside the proposed optimal concentration range would confirm the stated boundary rather than falsify the optimal-range hypothesis.
